{{Quote|This is only a stone, though it is smoothed and sharpened to a midnight point, but look closer. Each of its facets shows a single point of light. It might be the glint of firelight. It might be each a different Star.|The Colours of the Old Fire}}
[[The Flint]] was one of the [[Hours]]. It was one of the six Gods-from-Stone, who came into being before humanity, and one of the five among them who were cast down by the other Hours in [[the Lithomachy]]. When humanity was young, it learned the arts of shaping and remaking from The Flint, and the principle of {{Lore|Forge}} was once called "Flint". According to [[In Memory of Gods]], The Flint met its demise at the hands of [[The Forge of Days]], which first eclipsed it and then shattered it. This may correspond with [[Rites#Rite of the Rebel Striving|the Rite of the Rebel Striving]], a teaching of the Forge in which an artisan shatters a tool, which would later come to be associated with [[The Lionsmith]]'s shattering of his sword and betrayal of [[The Colonel]]. If this is the case, it suggests that the Forge's killing of Flint was a betrayal. The Flint was sent to [[Nowhere]] with the other dead [[Hours]].
